76: fn parse_name_value_opt<'a>(opts: &mut Options<'a>, opt: &'a OsStr) -> UResult<bool> {
77:     // is it a NAME=VALUE like opt ?
78:     let wrap = NativeStr::<'a>::new(opt);
79:     let split_o = wrap.split_once(&'=');
80:     if let Some((name, value)) = split_o {
81:         // yes, so push name, value pair
82:         opts.sets.push((name, value));
83:         Ok(false)
84:     } else {
85:         // no, it's a program-like opt
86:         parse_program_opt(opts, opt).map(|_| true)
87:     }

93:             125,

103:     // NOTE: config files are parsed using an INI parser b/c it's available and compatible with ".env"-style files
104:     //   ... * but support for actual INI files, although working, is not intended, nor claimed
105:     for &file in &opts.files {
106:         let conf = if file == "-" {
107:             let stdin = io::stdin();
108:             let mut stdin_locked = stdin.lock();
109:             Ini::read_from(&mut stdin_locked)
110:         } else {
111:             Ini::load_from_file(file)
112:         };

114:         let conf =
115:             conf.map_err(|e| USimpleError::new(1, format!("{}: {}", file.maybe_quote(), e)))?;

118:             // ignore all INI section lines (treat them as comments)
119:             for (key, value) in prop {
120:                 env::set_var(key, value);
121:             }
122:         }
123:     }

265:         macro_rules! map_parser_err {
266:             ($err:expr) => {{
267:                 let err = $err;
268:                 let pos = match err.err_type {
269:                     ErrorType::EndOfInput | ErrorType::InternalError => err.peek_position,
270:                 };
271:                 parse_error::ParseError::InternalError { pos, sub_err: err }
272:             }};
273:         }

275:         macro_rules! current_char {
276:             () => {{
277:                 let parser = &iterator.expander.parser;
278:                 if parser.remaining.is_empty() || parser.pointer >= parser.input.len() {
279:                     None
280:                 } else {
281:                     match parser.peek() {
282:                         Ok(c) => Some(c),
283:                         Err(err) => {
284:                             match err.err_type {
285:                                 ErrorType::EndOfInput => None,
286:                                 ErrorType::InternalError => return Err(map_parser_err!(err)),
287:                             }
288:                         }
289:                     }
290:                 }
291:             }};
292:         }
293: 
294:         macro_rules! skip_one {
295:             () => {{
296:                 if let Err(err) = iterator
297:                     .expander
298:                     .parser
299:                     .consume_one_ascii_or_all_non_ascii()
300:                 {
301:                     return Err(map_parser_err!(err));
302:                 }
303:             }};
304:         }
305: 
306:         macro_rules! take_one {
307:             () => {{
308:                 match iterator
309:                     .expander
310:                     .parser
311:                     .consume_one_ascii_or_all_non_ascii()
312:                 {
313:                     Ok(chunks) => {
314:                         for chunk in chunks {
315:                             match chunk {
316:                                 Chunk::InvalidEncoding(invalid) => {
317:                                     iterator.expander.output.extend(invalid)
318:                                 }
319:                                 Chunk::ValidSingleIntChar((_c, ni)) => {
320:                                     iterator.expander.output.push(ni)
321:                                 }
322:                             }
323:                         }
324:                     }
325:                     Err(err) => return Err(map_parser_err!(err)),
326:                 }
327:             }};
328:         }

330:         macro_rules! push_char {
331:             ($c:expr) => {{
332:                 let os_str = OsString::from($c.to_string());
333:                 let native = to_native_int_representation(&os_str);
334:                 iterator.expander.output.extend(native.deref());
335:             }};
336:         }

338:         macro_rules! push_word {
339:             () => {{
340:                 let word = mem::take(&mut iterator.expander.output);
341:                 iterator.words.push(word);
342:             }};
343:         }
344: 
345:         macro_rules! replace_escape {
346:             ($c:expr) => {{
347:                 if let Some((_, repl)) = REPLACEMENTS.iter().copied().find(|&(k, _)| k == $c) {
348:                     skip_one!();
349:                     push_char!(repl);

363:             };
364:         }

366:         macro_rules! substitute_variable {
367:             () => {{
368:                 let mut var_parse = VariableParser {
369:                     parser: &mut iterator.expander.parser,
370:                 };
371:                 let (name, default) = var_parse.parse_variable()?;
372:                 let varname_os = from_native_int_representation(Cow::Borrowed(name));

890:     /// Determines escaping style to use.
891:     fn escape_style(s: &str) -> EscapeStyle {
892:         if s.is_empty() {
893:             return EscapeStyle::SingleQuoted;
894:         }
895: 
896:         let mut special = false;
897:         let mut newline = false;
898:         let mut single_quote = false;
899: 
900:         for c in s.chars() {
901:             match c {
902:                 '\n' => {
903:                     newline = true;
904:                     special = true;
905:                 }
906:                 '\'' => {
907:                     single_quote = true;
908:                     special = true;
909:                 }
910:                 '|' | '&' | ';' | '<' | '>' | '(' | ')' | '$' | '`' | '\\' | '"' | ' ' | '\t'
911:                 | '*' | '?' | '[' | '#' | '˜' | '=' | '%' => {
912:                     special = true;
913:                 }
914:                 _ => continue,
915:             }
916:         }
917: 
918:         if !special {
919:             EscapeStyle::None
920:         } else if newline && !single_quote {
921:             EscapeStyle::SingleQuoted
922:         } else {
923:             EscapeStyle::Mixed

927:     /// Escapes special characters in a string, so that it will retain its literal
928:     /// meaning when used as a part of command in Unix shell.
929:     ///
930:     /// It tries to avoid introducing any unnecessary quotes or escape characters,
931:     /// but specifics regarding quoting style are left unspecified.
932:     pub fn quote(s: &str) -> std::borrow::Cow<str> {
933:         // We are going somewhat out of the way to provide
934:         // minimal amount of quoting in typical cases.
935:         match escape_style(s) {
936:             EscapeStyle::None => s.into(),
937:             EscapeStyle::SingleQuoted => format!("'{}'", s).into(),
938:             EscapeStyle::Mixed => {
939:                 let mut quoted = String::new();
940:                 quoted.push('\'');
941:                 for c in s.chars() {
942:                     if c == '\'' {
943:                         quoted.push_str("'\\''");
944:                     } else {
945:                         quoted.push(c);
946:                     }
947:                 }
948:                 quoted.push('\'');
949:                 quoted.into()
950:             }
951:         }
952:     }
